generator_metadata.summary: 0-bg grid (h~5-10, w~8-16) with 2-5 ENDPOINT PAIRS placed on distinct rows. Each pair places two SAME-COLOR cells on the SAME ROW at columns c1 < c2 with at least 1 empty cell between them. Different pairs use distinct non-bg colors. Rule: for every row that contains exactly two same-color cells at columns c1 < c2, FILL every cell at columns c1+1 .. c2-1 in that row with the pair's color (CONNECT the endpoints into a solid HORIZONTAL BAR). Endpoints stay; other rows untouched. Net: each pair of isolated row endpoints becomes a continuous colored horizontal line spanning the gap.

## 539d4ac45311 — defect to repair

The generator advertised `span_count` through 10 although ARC has only nine nonzero colors, while its explicit override path silently rejected counts above five. The repair changes the declared axis to 1–9 and adds an override-aware draw helper: normal random generation retains the prior difficulty bands, while explicit tests and downstream callers can exercise every lawful count through nine.

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The exact input-dependent grid after horizontal completion, together with the cells newly painted by that pass.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Detect every same-color horizontal endpoint pair whose strict interior is zero, then paint each complete horizontal span.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Read that completed grid and detect and paint every lawful same-color vertical endpoint span.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The vertical pass reads the completed grid: cells created by A can become vertical endpoints, fill whole columns between newly aligned bars, or occupy a crossing and block a competing vertical span. B therefore cannot be fixed from the original input alone.
